intro_html: Somebody figured out that everything good about an egg roll is on the inside, and the wrapper is mostly a delivery vehicle. So here it is without the wrapper: ground turkey and cabbage in a soy and ginger pan sauce, served over rice. It is a fifteen minute skillet that scales to fourteen containers, and it lands at 568 calories and 25 grams of protein for about $1.21, which is the cheapest bowl in this whole batch.
cost_closing_html: About $1.21 a bowl. Cabbage is the reason. Nothing else in the produce section gives you that much food for that little money.
shop_smart: Green cabbage is the cheapest vegetable in the store by weight and it is not close. Two heads fill this entire skillet for pocket change. Buy whole heads, never the bagged slaw, which charges you triple for the knife work.
A whole cabbage keeps for weeks in the fridge, so buy an extra when they are cheap. It is the one vegetable that does not punish you for planning ahead.
Soy sauce, rice vinegar, and brown sugar are the entire sauce and together they cost almost nothing for this batch. That is what a pantry does for you.
The ground turkey is over half the batch cost, so it is the one line worth timing to a sale. Everything else here is already priced like a rounding error.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Shred the cabbage thin and slice the onion. Do this before you turn the stove on, because once the pan is hot this dish moves fast.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and brown sugar together in a small bowl so the sauce is ready to pour.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or a wide pot over medium-high, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the sliced onion and the minced garlic and cook 3 minutes until fragrant.
Pile in the cabbage. It will look like too much and then it will cook down by half in about 6 minutes. Stir it often and stop while it still has some bite left.
Pour in the sauce, toss everything to coat, and cook 2 minutes more so the liquid clings instead of pooling in the bottom.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and slice the green onions for the top.
portion_html: Set the pot of rice on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is the rice bed for each container. Then divide the turkey and cabbage evenly across all 14, stirring the skillet between scoops so the meat does not settle to the bottom, and finish each with green onions. Every bowl lands at 568 calories and 25 grams of protein.

steps: Shred the cabbage and slice the onion.
Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, and brown sugar into a sauce.
Brown the ground turkey in vegetable oil to 165F, then add onion and garlic.
Add the cabbage and cook about 6 minutes until wilted but still crisp.
Pour in the sauce and toss 2 minutes to coat.
Cook the rice, portion by weight into 14 containers, and top with the skillet mixture and green onions.
